messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Re: gl.ibd function
parts:
Hi Athanasia,

 

This looks like a coordinate error (or you do not have at two individuals per population in you data set ).

 

Can you please check:

 

gl.map.interactive(gl5b)

 

if that works (these is the check the coordinates are set correctly)

 

and then

 

table(pop(gl5b))

 

to check your population definition.

 

 

Can you report back what you get there?

 

Cheers, Bernd

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Re: gl.ibd function
parts:
Hi Athanasia,

 

If you want to do an ibd over individuals you need to use a non interpopulation measure as the genetic distance (so no Fst as this requires populations).

 

You can use 1-gl.propShared as a distance, the proportion of shared alleles (which is often used for individuals).

 

So far gl.ibd does not do that automatically for you (wait for the next update). So you need to do by “hand”:

 

Eg.

 

Gdis <- 1-gl.propShared(gl5b)   #individuals distances

 

Edis <- as.matrix(dist(gl5b@other$latlong))  #distance matrix, technically you should project coordinates first but depending on the scale you are working if that is necessary

 

 

Then you can simply plot via

 

plot(as.dist(Edis), as.dist(Gdis))

and if you want a regression line:

 

abline(lm(as.dist(Gdis)~ as.dist(Edis)))

 

and your mantel test:

(e.g. from package ade4)

 

library(ade4)

mantel.randtest(as.dist(Gdis), as.dist(Edis))

 

 

Be aware I did not test the code, so there might be types, but in principle that should work.

Cheers, Bernd
